readme: REVIEWED ADDITIONS to the Hy-Vee catalogue - the third work-list source for pull-regular-hyvee.ps1. That puller is a REFRESH, not a pull: its work list is yesterday's own hyvee-regular file plus the Hy-Vee entries in product-urls.json, so a product that is in neither can never enter (1,538 rows is a fixed point, and 89.3% of the catalogue is absent). This file is the only way a NEW product joins that list, and the only writer is adjudicate-discovery.ps1 -Accept, which demands a named reviewer and written evidence. Every entry carries the productId Hy-Vee publishes, so the price is fetched from the store's own API exactly like every other row - nothing here supplies a price, a size or a board cell. Sizes are deliberately NOT stored: the puller's own header records that Hy-Vee's size field reports one unit of a multipack ('12 fl oz Cans' for a 12-pack) and mislabels ounces as counts, so an added product takes the same never-priced-before path every other new product takes, and the multipack and basis guards police it there.

items.name: That's Smart! Fold & Close Sandwich Bags
items.evidence: That's Smart! Fold and Close Sandwich Bags, 150 ct $1.29. Hy-Vee's value label, same per-bag basis as the Kroger 150 ct it beats, and cheaper than the Hy-Vee brand row already held at $2.29.
items.seen_at_discovery: $1.29 / 150 ct = $0.0086/each against a held $0.0153 - EVIDENCE ONLY, the puller re-derives both

items.name: JENNIE-O Turkey Bacon, 12 OZ
items.evidence: JENNIE-O Turkey Bacon against Butterball turkey bacon already held and Appleton Farms at Aldi. Right product. Accept adds it to the pull work list where the size is re-derived from the store, so the size is proven before it can price anything.
items.seen_at_discovery: $4.39 / 16 oz = $0.2744/oz against a held $0.3325 - EVIDENCE ONLY, the puller re-derives both
